headline: GTA VI pre-orders are live, PLS surges 3.5% on lithium optimism, and oil crashes nearly 4% on Hormuz reopening fears easing — big night ahead for US markets.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a strong session today, up 3.5% to $5.66. Lithium stocks got a lift from renewed interest in the sector — analysts at Kalkine are calling it a potential comeback play, and Pilbara is increasing spend on its P2000 expansion project. Still down 16% from your cost base, but today's move is a positive signal.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO slipped 1.2% last night despite the massive news that Rockstar officially opened GTA VI pre-orders at $80–$100 USD. The dip likely reflects investors locking in gains after earlier excitement — the stock is still up 4.5% overall on your position. The $80 base / $100 premium pricing is higher than GTA V, which is good for revenue per unit.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google had a solid session last night, up 1% to $349.61. No specific news drove the move — it rode broader NASDAQ strength, which gained 0.66%. Your position is now 13.7% in the green.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI closed up 1% today to $17.97 — AI sentiment remains strong on the ASX, tracking the positive tech mood from Wall Street. Still sitting about 4.85% below your cost base, but trending the right way.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.54% today to $527.36, reflecting last night's US market strength (S&P 500 up 0.6%). Now 2.3% above your cost base — a quiet but steady performer.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged up 0.22% today to $76.90 — broad market tailwinds doing the work here. Up 2% overall on your position.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL dipped 0.37% today to $8.13 as oil prices took a hammering — crude (WTI) fell nearly 4% last night after the Strait of Hormuz (a key shipping chokepoint for Middle East oil) reportedly reopened, easing fears of a supply crunch. Macquarie has also slashed its oil price outlook dramatically. This is a headwind for energy ETFs.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.35% today to $94.67 — essentially flat. The Aussie dollar fell 1.4% against the USD, which can affect emerging market ETF pricing. Nearly at breakeven overall (up just 0.09% on your position).

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was basically flat last night, down just 0.05% to $373.74. The big news was a 20-year power deal with Chevron to supply electricity for a new AI data centre in West Texas — a sign of Microsoft's massive long-term bet on AI infrastructure. Still down 15.7% on your position overall.

watch_today.title: GTA VI pre-orders live — $80–$100 price point confirmed
watch_today.detail: Rockstar Games officially opened pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI last night at $80 (standard) and $100 (premium), higher than GTA V's launch price. This is the biggest revenue catalyst in gaming this decade. TTWO dipped 1.2% last night — possibly profit-taking — but the underlying story is bullish. Hold through to the late-2025/2026 launch window.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX up 3.5% today — lithium showing signs of life
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals had its best session in a while, closing up 3.47% to $5.66. Multiple analysts are flagging a potential lithium sector recovery, and PLS is ramping up its P2000 expansion spend. You're still 16% underwater on this one, but momentum is improving. Worth watching for a few more positive sessions before adding more.

watch_today.title: Oil crashes 4% — big headwind for FUEL.AX
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil fell from $73.21 to $70.45 last night (down 3.77%) after the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which about 20% of the world's oil flows — reportedly reopened, reducing fears of a supply squeeze. Macquarie has also dramatically cut its oil price forecast. This is a direct negative for your FUEL.AX energy ETF, which tracks global oil and gas companies.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike fears heating up — watch your mortgage and bond-heavy holdings
watch_today.detail: Australia's underlying inflation (the 'trimmed mean' measure the RBA focuses on) came in hotter than expected, with multiple economists warning the Reserve Bank may need to raise interest rates again rather than cut them. This is bad news for borrowers and for growth-oriented assets. Keep an eye on VDHG, which holds bonds — rate hikes reduce bond values.

watch_today.title: Gold falls 2.5% — safe-haven selling as risk mood improves
watch_today.detail: Gold dropped from $4,129 to $4,027 per ounce last night (down 2.49%). When investors feel more confident about markets, they sell gold (which pays no income) and move into shares. This isn't directly in your portfolio, but it signals a broader 'risk-on' mood that's generally good for equities like GOOG and VTS.

watch_today.title: MSFT lands 20-year power deal for AI data centre in West Texas
watch_today.detail: Microsoft signed a 20-year electricity supply deal with Chevron to power a massive new AI data centre in West Texas. This kind of long-term infrastructure commitment shows Microsoft is serious about scaling its AI capabilities — a positive long-term signal for the stock even if it's been a drag on your portfolio lately. Hold.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ finished solidly in the green — the S&P gained 0.6% to a fresh high of 7,409 and the NASDAQ rose 0.66% to 25,755. The big story underneath was a sharp sell-off in oil (down 3.8%) and gold (down 2.5%), suggesting investors moved out of 'safety' assets and back into shares. The Aussie dollar dropped 1.4% against the USD to 68.96 cents, meaning your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) are worth a little less in AUD terms than the raw price moves suggest. ASX 200 data was unavailable for today's close.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is inflation — underlying inflation came in hotter than expected, putting the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) back in the spotlight with markets now pricing in the possibility of another interest rate rise rather than a cut. Separately, the Albanese government is copping heat on two fronts: procurement laws seen as favouring the construction union (CFMEU), and its own human rights committee knocking back NDIS reform legislation.

stories.title: Hot inflation data puts RBA rate hike back on the table
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's 'core' inflation — which strips out volatile items to show the underlying trend — came in above expectations, catching economists off guard. Multiple forecasters are now warning the RBA may need to raise interest rates again (or at minimum, delay any cuts) rather than ease off. This is bad news for mortgage holders and anyone with variable-rate debt. It also pushed the Aussie dollar around — initially up on rate hike bets, but the broader economic uncertainty weighed on it later.

stories.title: Labor accused of 'rigging procurement' to favour CFMEU construction union
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is pushing through changes to federal procurement rules (the rules that govern how the government awards contracts) that business groups say would give the CFMEU construction union an unfair advantage in bidding for government work. The AFR reports Labor is rushing the laws through before financial year end. Business groups are calling it a move that 'sows the seeds of corruption' — strong language that signals this will be a political fight heading into the second term.

stories.title: Labor's own human rights committee knocks back NDIS reform bill
stories.why_it_matters: In an embarrassing own goal, a Labor-dominated parliamentary human rights committee has recommended against passing the government's own NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) reform bill, saying it doesn't adequately protect participants' rights. This puts the legislation in doubt and adds to a growing list of internal tensions for the Albanese government in its second term. NDIS reform is critical for budget sustainability — the scheme's costs have been blowing out for years.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by regulatory themes — governments and regulators globally are scrambling to keep up with AI moving faster than the law. There's also a big hardware story: Broadcom and OpenAI are teaming up to build a custom AI processor chip, which is a direct challenge to Nvidia's dominance. And ByteDance (TikTok's parent) is about to drop an upgraded AI video model.

stories.title: Broadcom and OpenAI partner to build a custom AI processor chip
stories.why_it_matters: Broadcom has announced it's working with OpenAI to build a custom AI chip specifically designed for running large language models (the technology behind ChatGPT). This matters because right now Nvidia basically has a monopoly on the AI chip market, and every major tech company is trying to reduce their dependence on it. A Broadcom-OpenAI chip could shake up the AI hardware landscape — good news for anyone holding AI-themed ETFs like GXAI.AX, and worth watching for Nvidia's response.

stories.title: ByteDance targeting July launch for upgraded AI video model
stories.why_it_matters: TikTok's parent company ByteDance is planning to launch an upgraded AI video generation model in July 2026. AI video — the ability to generate realistic video clips from text prompts — is one of the hottest battlegrounds in AI right now, with OpenAI's Sora and Google's Veo also competing. A ByteDance entry raises the competitive stakes and signals that AI-generated video is moving from novelty to a real commercial product fast.

stories.title: UK's FCA warns AI is moving faster than financial regulation can keep up
stories.why_it_matters: The head of the UK's Financial Conduct Authority (the main financial regulator) has publicly warned that AI is advancing so quickly that existing laws simply can't keep up. This is a global theme right now — Greece opened public consultation on an AI regulation bill today, and Bloomberg ran a piece on the messy regulatory saga around Anthropic (maker of Claude). For investors in AI stocks and ETFs, regulatory uncertainty is a real risk — new laws could suddenly restrict how AI products are used or sold in major markets.

stories.title: Bloomberg: The Anthropic saga shows the wrong way to regulate AI
stories.why_it_matters: Bloomberg's opinion piece uses the controversy around Anthropic — the AI safety startup backed by Google and Amazon — as a case study in how NOT to regulate AI. The piece argues that heavy-handed, company-specific interventions create confusion and undermine innovation without actually making AI safer. This feeds into a broader debate about whether governments globally will land on sensible AI rules or create a patchwork of conflicting regulations that hamper the industry.

sport.summary: NRL Round 17 kicks off tomorrow night with Eels vs Rabbitohs at CommBank Stadium. AFL trade and team news dominated today — Collingwood is pushing to change the AFL pre-game format, the Swans made a surprise ruck selection, and NRLW signings continue to flow. Wimbledon is also just around the corner with young Aussie Joanna Garland flagging her dream to play the tournament.

stories.title: NRL Round 17 preview — Titans host Bulldogs at Cbus Super Stadium on Friday
stories.why_it_matters: Round 17 tips are in — your local Titans host the Bulldogs Friday at 6pm at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast. The Broncos then face the Roosters at Suncorp at 8pm Friday night. Dolphins take on the Warriors Saturday at 3pm, also at Suncorp. Sharks are on a bye this round.

stories.title: Swans make surprise ruck call as key players return for AFL Round 16
stories.why_it_matters: Sydney Swans have named a surprise ruck selection for this week's AFL match, with a key duo also returning from injury. No specific player names were available in the article text, but it's a notable selection shakeup heading into the back half of the season.

stories.title: Collingwood pushing to revolutionise AFL pre-game format
stories.why_it_matters: Collingwood are reportedly leading a push to change the AFL's pre-game format — the details aren't fully public yet but it appears to involve changes to the pre-match entertainment or warm-up structure. Collingwood as a club tend to get what they want when they push for rule changes, so this one's worth watching.

stories.title: Wests Tigers ink deal with replacement for Jarome Luai
stories.why_it_matters: The Wests Tigers have continued their busy off-season recruiting drive, signing a halfback to replace Jarome Luai who departed for the Cowboys. The Tigers are clearly in rebuild mode — they've been on a signing spree as they try to rebuild their roster around a new halves combination.
